page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The system features 192 dedicated physical cores using AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors clocked at 2.7 GHz, operating without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 1536.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core allocation. Local high-speed storage is integrated directly via 11400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No hardware GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results illustrate substantial parallel processing throughput alongside robust memory access. In multi-core tests, the 192-core setup registers top-tier ratings in stress-ng multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory throughput is exceptionally high, reaching 895.63 GB/sec in uncached read-only tests and 411.52 GB/sec in large-block writes. Real-world key-value execution shows notable capacity, with Redis SET operations achieving 361.71 million operations per second and PassMark database operations ranking in the top tier. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including single-core Geekbench and single-core stress-ng, remain in the average tier.

The architecture delivers high compute and memory density per socket, providing cost efficiency for heavily threaded workloads that can scale across ARM64 cores without hyperthreading contention. However, applications dependent on x86 vector extensions or single-threaded clock speed will experience tradeoffs. The vast 1.5 TB memory footprint paired with 11.4 TB of low-latency NVMe SSD makes this instance suitable for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis or Memcached clusters, real-time analytics engines, distributed caching tiers, and data-intensive ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.48xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based server powered by 192 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.7 GHz without multithreading. Equipped with 1536.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and 11400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, it pairs high-capacity volatile memory with fast local scratch space alongside 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-threaded scaling and memory bandwidth, evidenced by over 361 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier multi-core stress-ng scores. Single-core performance falls in the average category, making throughput dependent on parallelism. Without GPU acceleration, the platform offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for highly concurrent, memory-heavy workloads that run natively on ARM64. It is designed for massive in-memory databases, distributed caching, enterprise search indices, and large-scale data processing pipelines requiring extensive memory capacity and fast ephemeral storage.
